LHX.sentence: L3Harris barely moved today, and while its profit margins are running below the other big defense contractors as it digests the Aerojet rocket-motor acquisition, steady military spending keeps the underlying business on solid footing.

ASML.sentence: ASML dipped slightly and looks less expensive than it first appears, since the only maker of these advanced chipmaking machines is in a temporary earnings lull that should pass.

LIN.sentence: Linde had a soft day, but the quiet reliability of selling oxygen and nitrogen on long contracts is the whole point — and it's unusually not commanding its typical premium right now.

MSFT.sentence: Microsoft is quiet — it's lagged the hottest AI names a touch lately, but the Azure cloud and AI story just keeps grinding along without drama.

TMO.sentence: Thermo Fisher slipped a few percent, though biotech funding is thawing, and since that money leads to lab-equipment orders a couple of quarters later, the backdrop is slowly improving.

ENB.sentence: Enbridge is steady and pays a hefty dividend, though with interest rates high right now that generous payout looks merely fair rather than a standout bargain.

NOW.sentence: ServiceNow bounced today and now sits well below its peak; corporations and government agencies keep signing up for its workflow and AI-assistant tools on long contracts.

GLNCY.sentence: Glencore held its ground while copper prices sagged, because its giant commodity-trading arm cushions the blow when any single metal weakens.

MLM.sentence: Martin Marietta is flat, and the price it gets per ton of crushed stone is still creeping upward — the headline price drop is just a quirk of what mix of products sold, not real weakness.

KOF.sentence: Coca-Cola FEMSA slipped a bit, mostly on currency wobble since most of its earnings come from Mexico, but nothing has actually changed about how much Coke it's selling across Latin America.

PBR.A.sentence: Petrobras ticked up, and with oil selling far above what it costs them to pull out of the ground, there's plenty of cash flowing to fund its very large dividend.

AMKBY.sentence: Maersk, the container-shipping giant that moves goods around the world, is down a touch, but the shares trade for less than it would cost to replace its fleet of ships — a solid floor under the price.

MA.sentence: Mastercard slipped a little and is unusually priced right in line with rival Visa, with nothing specific gone wrong — people just keep tapping their cards more than ever.

ISRG.sentence: The da Vinci surgical-robot maker fell again and sits well off its high, but that looks like nervousness rather than real trouble — hospitals aren't doing fewer operations with its machines.
